children: Court cites airline’s failure to honour its commitment to deposit Rs 50 crore as it rejects an alternative security proposal in the dispute with former promoter Kalanithi Maran and KAL Airways

The Delhi High Court has rejected SpiceJet’s plea to offer a Gurugram property as security instead of depositing Rs 144.51 crore in its ongoing legal dispute with former promoter Kalanithi Maran and KAL Airways.

The court said repeated extensions could not be granted after the airline failed to honour its undertaking to deposit Rs 50 crore within 45 days. SpiceJet had proposed furnishing documents for a one-acre land parcel in Udyog Vihar, Gurugram, in place of the cash deposit.
The property was valued by the airline at Rs 400-500 crore. However, the court declined to accept the proposal, reiterating the requirement for a monetary deposit.
Court Flags Failure To Meet Payment Commitment
SpiceJet had undertaken on July 13, 2026, to deposit Rs 50 crore with the court registry within 45 days and pay the remaining Rs 94.51 crore within 90 days.

The undertaking was linked to the airline’s expectation of receiving funds under the Centre’s Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS 5.0). The airline had cited the proposed financial support as a means of meeting its payment obligations while maintaining operations.
The court observed that it could have considered taking a lenient view on the timeline for the second instalment if SpiceJet had complied with its initial commitment to deposit Rs 50 crore.

It rejected the request for further extensions, noting that the airline had failed to fulfil its own undertaking. The enforcement applications in the matter are scheduled to be heard on November 3, 2026.
Dispute Stems From Share Transfer Agreement

The legal dispute concerns the transfer of SpiceJet shares from Maran and KAL Airways to Ajay Singh in February 2015. The former promoters had transferred their 58.46 per cent stake in the airline to Singh.
Maran and KAL Airways subsequently sought the transfer of 180 million warrants that could be converted into equity shares. The dispute was referred to arbitration in 2016.
In July 2018, the arbitral tribunal rejected Maran’s claim for Rs 1,323 crore in damages over the non-issuance of warrants but awarded a refund of Rs 579 crore, along with interest.
The subsequent legal proceedings have involved challenges to the arbitral award and directions concerning the amounts payable by SpiceJet and Singh.
